title: 2025 budget for local boards and shared services
subtitle: Police resources for intimate partner violence and trafficking, county social services costs, library staffing, and The Elliott loan.
overview: Council approved the 2025 budget update for local boards and shared services agencies, completing the 2025 budget process {{vote:m1}}. It covers Guelph Police Services, the Guelph Public Library, the County of Wellington's social services, public health, The Elliott Community, the Downtown Guelph Business Association and the Grand River Conservation Authority. The approved net levy requirement is up to $351,105,144, an increase of $10,117,959 or 3.12 per cent over 2024 for these agencies.

Council also authorized staff to sign a fixed-term loan agreement of about $2.5 million with The Elliott for its 29-bed long-term care expansion {{vote:m2}}. After the vote, staff and the mayor said the total tax impact for 2025 is 6.78 per cent. They said it would have been 10.51 per cent without the city-side reductions.

Most of the meeting was presentations and questions. Police asked for added staff for intimate partner violence, human trafficking, fraud and child exploitation. The county described rising housing and homelessness costs for the city. The library described staffing for the new central library, which is due to open in 2026.

decisions.item: Local boards and shared services budget
decisions.detail: Council approved the amended 2025 operating budget for the local boards and shared services agencies, with a net levy increase of $10,117,959 or 3.12 per cent over 2024.
The approved budget includes an increased net levy requirement for Guelph Police Services of $5,142,214 over 2024.
The approved budget includes an increased net levy requirement for the County of Wellington of $4,528,954 over 2024.
Council approved a $624,346 net levy increase for the library and acknowledged a $1,634,000 debt funding transfer between the City and library budgets, with no net effect on the levy.
Council approved a net levy requirement of up to $351,105,144, a Downtown Guelph Business Association levy of $721,200, and a local boards capital budget with gross spending of $7,004,308.
Staff are authorized to execute a fixed-term loan of about $2.5 million with The Elliott for the 29-bed long-term care expansion, subject to the City Treasurer and City Solicitor being satisfied.

debate: Police and a delegate from the force said intimate partner violence, human trafficking and child exploitation are under-resourced. They said that two-thirds of child exploitation tips could not be investigated and that fraud cases wait one to two years in the queue.

One councillor asked how much of the police increase would go to prevention and education. Police said six new positions would go to the intimate partner violence and human trafficking unit, and they committed to funding public awareness work. Another councillor said the police budget should be compared with those of other forces along the 401.

County staff said the city's social services cost increase reflects housing and homelessness pressures, a phased-in 2024 increase and low provincial Ontario Works rates. Councillors asked about shelter capacity, supportive housing and the lack of a plan for new social housing in the city. Staff said there is no capital plan for new social housing yet.

Library staff said the new central library requires added staff and a one-time collection purchase funded by development charges. A councillor asked whether this was a surprise cost, and staff said it was expected and does not affect the tax rate.
A councillor noted that the police presentations included distressing accounts shared without a warning. Police agreed to send out a link to victim services.
